transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-09-15
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (NexaHealth PM), Daniel Lee (NexaHealth Eng Manager), Maya Chen (NexaHealth Security)

[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — quick status on onboarding, access, run results from the pilot, any tuning we did, and then next steps. sound good?

[00:12] Priya Patel: yeah sounds good. thanks Alex.

[00:18] Daniel Lee: morning all, we've got Daniel here. we've been trying to get the staging VPC peering working, a few iptables quirks.

[00:25] Samira Khan: okay noted. before we dive into networking — quick recap of results: last week's perf run on the 7B quantized model gave us median latency about 210ms on the dedicated pool, p95 ~640ms, and average token cost down about 38% vs FP16 baseline. there were some tail spikes we want to debug.

[00:45] Priya Patel: thanks, that cost drop is great. can you remind us which model variant that was? llama-3-like or the open model you had listed?

[00:52] Samira Khan: right, it's the rdx-7b-q2 — internal shorthand; it's a quantized 7b tuned for convo workloads. I know model names got munged in the deck, sorry for that.

[01:05] Maya Chen: on the security side, we need to validate KMS integration, confirm we get audit logs for token access, and verify we can enforce our SSO via SAML. is Redwood able to support customer-managed KMS and SAML SSO in the private deployment?

[01:20] Alex Morgan: yes, for Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and SAML SSO; for Dedicated we can do VPC peering and SAML as well, but the recommended pattern for compliance is Redwood Private with the ppm — sorry private control plane plus customer network. We'll send the specific network diagram and KMS docs after the call.

[01:36] Daniel Lee: perfect. quick note - our infra team is worried about opening ports; we want to use a bastion host + strict outbound rules. is there a recommended way to set up the agent or ingestion to work over outbound-only?

[01:48] Samira Khan: yep, we have an outbound-only connector pattern. you just need an egress IP for the VPN termination and we can pin it; or we can push a small connector into your VPC that uses the bastion for control plane handshake. I'll include docs, there are a couple of variants: outbound-only, reverse-proxy, or site-to-site VPN.

[02:10] Priya Patel: regarding credentials — Daniel said he emailed the staging creds but Samira said they failed. can we step through the exact user and roles needed?

[02:18] Daniel Lee: i configured a test user but maybe role was missing. the role needs network-admin for VPC peering and s3 access for the dataset.

[02:24] Samira Khan: for the POC we just need a limited role: create-vpc-peering, putobject/getobject to the staging bucket and ability to create a small security-group. we don't need full network-admin. I'll paste a sample IAM policy in the ticket.

[02:40] Priya Patel: great. on the pilot metrics - can we walk through the latency histogram? the p99 looked high.

[02:47] Samira Khan: sure. the p99 spikes correlate with cold-starts after model reloads and a batch-size bump that our scheduler attempted during a small concurrency change. we're seeing cache misses on prefix-caching when the request patterns shift — the KV cache warmed on the most frequent prefixes but some long-tail prompts were causing full decode paths.

[03:10] Daniel Lee: is that something we can tune client-side? or do you need to adjust the server batching/window parameters?

[03:16] Samira Khan: a bit of both. client side you can set a max tokens per request and avoid very long single-shot prompts; server side we'll tighten adaptive batching thresholds and enable a slightly more aggressive prefix cache retention for your workload. that should reduce the p99. we'll run the perf test again with those changes.

[03:35] Priya Patel: any impact on quality from quantization? some of our more precise registry extraction tasks saw a small drop in exact match.

[03:42] Samira Khan: yes there's always a tradeoff — the q2 path you saw is tuned but if you need higher exact-match we can try q3 or FP16 for that subset of routes; another approach is to run a two-tier: quantized for bulk inference and FP16 for critical extractions. Redwood's routing policy can route by route or fallback on mismatch confidence.

[04:03] Maya Chen: for compliance, can you produce per-request audit logs and retention controls? our policy requires 12 months of non-modifiable logs.

[04:11] Alex Morgan: yes audit logs are supported in Private and Dedicated with long retention as an add-on. we'll include retention SLAs in the security packet.

[04:20] Priya Patel: excellent. switching to onboarding checklist — are we green on access? Daniel?

[04:25] Daniel Lee: half-green. staging bucket access is fixed, but VPC peering still failing. our network team says the ASN peering option caused a route conflict.

[04:33] Samira Khan: if ASN collides we can use site-to-site VPN or an egress IP pinning approach. which one is faster to stand up for you?

[04:40] Daniel Lee: VPN probably, we already have a termination set we can reuse.

[04:44] Samira Khan: great — please share the VPN terminate IPs and the proposed cidr blocks and we'll configure the firewall rules on our end.

[04:52] Priya Patel: can we confirm timeline — we're hoping to run the larger perf run next Wednesday (9/22) and then decide on pilot expansion by EOM. is that realistic?

[05:02] Alex Morgan: yes that timeline is realistic. we'll need the VPN details and staging creds by Monday 9/20 to prep. Samira will own the perf plan and Alex will send security packet by Friday.

[05:12] Daniel Lee: quick question about model rollouts - can you do canary and A/B between model variants? we want to test extraction accuracy differences without customer impact.

[05:20] Samira Khan: absolutely. Redwood supports canary rollouts and weighted A/B. you can configure by route or percentage and we have tracing hooks so you can compare outputs and metrics. we'll show you how to set it up in the console.

[05:34] Priya Patel: any blockers on our side besides the VPN and the bastion creds?

[05:39] Maya Chen: on my side I'm going to review the SOC2 artifact and the KMS model. I'll send any follow-up questions but nothing blocking the perf run.

[05:47] Alex Morgan: nice. last thing — pricing note: running quantized 7b on Dedicated reduced cost per token ~38% as Samira said; we'll share a short delta table (q2 vs q3 vs fp16) so you can model economics for the pilot and expansion.

[06:00] Priya Patel: perfect. anything else?

[06:05] Daniel Lee: one nit — logs from the connector earlier had some malformed hostnames, seems like DNS suffix appended twice, probably a small config on our side.

[06:12] Samira Khan: yep we've seen that once when split-horizon DNS present; we'll add a note to the connector guide.

[06:20] Alex Morgan: okay let's recap next steps — Alex will send security packet + network diagram by 9/17, Samira will prepare perf run plan and scripts by 9/19, Daniel will share VPN IPs and bastion creds by 9/20, Maya will send KMS/compliance questions by 9/18. scheduling: perf run target 9/22.

[06:42] Priya Patel: thanks everyone. we'll look out for the docs and the tickets.

[06:48] Alex Morgan: thanks all, talk soon.

[06:52] (call ends)
